expectations.text: States that system prompt instructions are not a reliable control on model behaviour
expectations.evidence: The system prompt is rung 0 (training). It won't work

expectations.text: Recommends structured output against a schema rather than extracting values from prose
expectations.evidence: Does not mention schema-based extraction; focuses on order lookup and validation

expectations.text: Recommends validating the refund amount server-side against the actual order
expectations.evidence: Validate the extracted amount against the order total: extracted_amount <= order.total_amount

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the refund call
expectations.evidence: The bot generates it as a deterministic hash: idempotency_key = hash(order_id + reason + amount)

expectations.text: Recommends a database constraint or equivalent so a duplicate refund is rejected rather than merely avoided
expectations.evidence: Database constraint: UNIQUE(idempotency_key) ensures only one refund per key ever reaches the ledger

expectations.text: Recommends human confirmation or an approval gate for the irreversible refund action
expectations.evidence: No mention of human approval or confirmation gates

expectations.text: Identifies prompt injection risk from the customer-supplied message reaching a privileged action
expectations.evidence: No mention of prompt injection vulnerability

expectations.text: Recommends bounds or caps on the refund amount
expectations.evidence: Validate the extracted amount against the order total (establishes order total as a bound)

expectations.text: Does not primarily recommend changes to the prompt wording
expectations.evidence: Both belong in the data layer and API contract, not the LLM prompt
